title: Triangulations of the Sphere
summary: Thurston gave a simple way to construct all triangulations of the sphere for which 5 or 6 triangles meet at each vertex, using the Eisenstein integers $\mathbb{E}$. While such triangulations can be defined purely combinatorially, Thurston noticed that given such a triangulation, one can make all the triangles into flat equilateral triangles with the same edge length, and this gives the 2-sphere a flat Riemannian metric except at 12 cone points with angle deficit $π/3$. He showed that up to rescaling, all such Riemannian metrics arise from his procedure. He studied the moduli space…
